notes: kb/Work PB5373 class 4, decided 2026-11-12. §1985:VII.4.7.4 GR14: a WRITE beyond "the externally defined boundaries of a sequential file" is an exception condition, the record area is unaffected, (a) the I-O status indicates a boundary violation and (b) the file's USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION declarative runs; (c) with no declarative "the result is undefined" and nothing is asserted for it. The boundary is the implementor's (§1985:VII.1.3.5 GRL2.3 b: "The implementor specifies the manner in which these boundaries are defined"), and docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-108 states it: the capacity of the host medium, answered at the WRITE with status 34 (FileStatusCode.ForWriteFailure classifies the host's refusal by HostFile.IsMediumBoundary). The witness SequentialWriteBoundaryTests runs an 85 program that writes a sequential file ASSIGNed to Linux's /dev/full (full by construction) with FILE STATUS and a USE procedure: FS=34, USE=1, and the record area still holds what the program set. The device exists on Linux only, so the test returns on a host that is not Linux (and fails if Linux lacks the device), the shape of FileBoundaryTests and ReportLineRefusalConformanceTests; the unit tests drive the connector the same way.

next.reason: Kept: §2023:14.9.51.4 GR20 (write beyond the externally-defined boundaries: unsuccessful, status '34', a boundary violation per §2023:9.1.13.6 GR4), §2023:14.9.51.4 GR15 (record area unaffected) and the USE procedure when one applies (§2023:14.9.49.4 GR6). Changed: 1985 c. 'If a USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION declarative is not ... specified ..., the result is undefined'. 2023 sends control through 9.1.12/9.1.13 (GR15), and §2023:9.1.13.1 makes 3x fatal: 'the implementor determines what action is taken ... The implementor may either continue or terminate the execution of the run unit. If the implementor chooses to continue execution of the run unit, control is transferred to the end of the statement'. Undefined became a bounded implementor choice. (The §2023:9.1.13.1 prose has no catalog rule id.)
